caption: The drawing depicts a brass-colored lantern with a rectangular structure and a slightly arched roof. At the top center of the lantern is a circular ring handle attached by a small spherical joint. The lantern has three visible glass panels, framed with brass strips, which allow a clear view of the interior. Inside the lantern, there is a cylindrical holder standing upright on a base, containing a white candle with melted wax visible running down one side. The back panel of the lantern’s interior appears to have a vertically ribbed, brass surface. The base of the lantern is hexagonal and has small vent holes along the bottom edge on each panel. To the upper left corner of the main drawing, there is a smaller sketch of the lantern with dimensions noted. The lantern is centered on a plain beige background, bounded by a faint rectangular border. The bottom right corner bears the inscription “James M. Linson” with an additional notation "Corodon Lantern, Dec. 1882."
title: Wardroom Lamp from "Constitution"
cluster: #16 — Lighting Devices: Lamps, Lanterns, and Candleholders
